title: Rights Entropy Visualizer and Access Repair Flow
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem: Admins at scale struggle to understand how a workspace's effective permissions diverge from intended policies. Existing audit lists show events and role assignments, but do not surface the 'entropy' — where small, drifting grants create high-risk combinations across service accounts, integrations, and temporal grants. This ticket proposes a Rights Entropy Visualizer (REV) that: 1) summarizes divergence between declared role policy and derived effective access; 2) surfaces hotspots where small user sets or integrations generate outsized privileges; and 3) provides an interactive Access Repair Flow (ARF) that guides admins through least-privilege remediations with safe rollouts and audit notes.
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity REV mockup in Figma covering workspace and org levels, including heatmap, entropy score, and sortable hotspot list
Clickable ARF prototype that demonstrates: propose-remediation -> simulated impact preview -> canary rollout plan -> generated audit note
Design sign-off from PM (Lena Hsu) and Security (Omar Singh) documented in comments
Handoff spec with tokens for accessibility, microcopy for confirmation flows, and edge-case error states uploaded to Confluence
Bench mocked analytics queries for estimated backend compute spikes attached to ticket (to inform ENG scope)
decisions: Represent entropy as a 0-100 score combining role divergence, cross-workspace grants, and service-account bindings; color scale chosen to align with console brand but ensure WCAG AA contrast
Show heatmap at two resolutions: per-resource-type and per-role; default to resource-type for broad triage
ARF will use a simulated dry-run mode that can be exported as an immutable audit note (no immediate changes unless user confirms rollout)
Cost view: include an estimated 'remediation effort' score (low/med/high) to help prioritize fixes alongside potential risk reduction
Rollout: integrate with existing Rollouts infrastructure (canary + staged escalation) rather than inventing a new scheduler
design_notes: Primary persona: workspace admin with 50-500 users and multiple service accounts; secondary: compliance officer auditing monthly

Key flows: 1) Identify hotspot from global dashboard; 2) Open hotspot detail; 3) Run ARF proposed changes; 4) Preview simulated login/access matrix post-change; 5) Authorize canary rollout with optional revert window
Controls: quick 'snooze' for low-risk hotspots, 'delegate' to team owners, and 'escalate' to security for high-entropy items
Microcopy: explain entropy metric on hover and in tooltip with one-sentence remediation guidance
Accessibility: keyboard-first interactions in ARF, explicit focus management for modal dialogs, and ARIA labels on heatmap cells
outstanding_risks: Backend cost: computing effective access for large orgs may require heavy graph traversals; ENG dependency to design sampling and caching strategy
False positives: naive heuristics could surface noise — require staged rollout of scoring algorithm with feedback collection
Operational: accidentally offering a 'one-click fix' could be abused; ARF must default to dry-run and require additional confirmation for live changes
Localization: entropy language is abstract; microcopy needs localization review to ensure clarity in APAC markets
